item.title: 'HyperBird' imaging platform spots grape diseases before they're visible
item.description: HyperBird, a cutting-edge imaging platform for observing microscopic traits in plants, can detect grape diseases—such as powdery and downy mildews, which cost vineyard owners billions in annual losses globally—days before physical symptoms become visible. The advancement could allow plant breeders to speed the development of disease-resistant grape varieties, cue growers to target fungicide use early in a disease's progression and provide vineyard workers with better, earlier information for crop management. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Supermassive black hole winds are 100 times more powerful than scientists thought
item.description: Astronomers have discovered that winds from a supermassive black hole are about 100 times more powerful than previously thought. XRISM observations showed the resulting turbulence spreading roughly 300,000 light-years, extending far beyond the black hole’s host galaxy. The energy involved rivals several billion supernova explosions, revealing just how dramatically black holes can influence the space around them. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why don't birds fall out of trees while sleeping? The unusual science behind the phenomenon
item.description: Birds have evolved unique adaptations that allow them to sleep safely on tree branches. Special tendon and leg structures automatically secure their feet when their legs bend, which maintains balance even in slightly moving branches. Some birds also utilize their foot shape and balance for perching, while others may choose to rest on one leg to conserve heat during colder weather. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
